name: U.S. Virgin Islands

law.summary: The territory runs its own NPDES program (TPDES, authorized 1976). No public-notice duty for overflows was found; VIWMA issues notices by press release in practice. The TPDES rules (12 VIRR ch. 184) were not read.

regulator_report.deadline: assumed 24 hours oral, 5 days written (federal standard condition)

erule.notes: VIWMA files through NeT-SewerOverflow for 3 of its 8 collection systems; nothing after 2026-06.

sso.notes: News carries more events than SOBE.

beaches.program: DPNR Beach Water Quality Monitoring Program
beaches.notes: Weekly text PDFs, found through the WordPress media API; lists failing and not-sampled beaches.

habs.notes: Sargassum is mentioned in advisory text.

barriers.what: VIWMA notices reach the public mainly through news outlets and social posts
VIWMA site reset connections from this machine
barriers.note: unconfirmed whether a block or an outage

readiness.rationale: SOBE gives a few dated events with points; the weekly DPNR beach PDF is the steadier signal. VIWMA's notices are scattered in news.

owner_questions: Accept a weekly PDF parse (DPNR beach advisories) as an advisory source?
SOBE has stopped at 2026-06 for VI: show the territory as 'Dated reports, delayed' anyway?
surprise: The Virgin Islands, unlike the other territories, issue their own NPDES permits (TPDES since 1976), yet their only dated overflow data is the 14 events VIWMA filed with EPA.
